dek: A football pick service run by a bettor known only as Payne, who co hosts the Bet The Board podcast with former oddsmaker Todd Fuhrman. The only package we could price was a 30 day NFL and college football pass at $579.99 through PayPal. All sales are final. His site posts season totals back to 2007, losing years included, and his three football headline numbers add up when we recount them, but there is no pick by pick log and we found no independent buyer reviews.

short_answer: Payne Insider is a real, long running pick service. The same Payne co hosts Bet The Board, a free NFL and college football betting podcast with former Caesars oddsmaker Todd Fuhrman. Apple Podcasts lists the show from 2014 to 2025 with about 300 episodes and a 4.8 rating, and in August 2026 it came back on Clay Travis's Sport & State under a three year deal, with Hard Rock Bet as presenting sponsor. Payne does not publish his last name, and the site gives no company name, address or phone number, only an email address.

The football page shows no prices in its text, but the PayPal button behind it sells one product on 20 Nov 2026: a 30 Day NFL + College Football package for $579.99. The terms say all sales are final, payment is earned once you log in, and nothing about performance is guaranteed.

The records page is more open than most. It lists every season since 2007 by sport, including losing ones. We added up every football line ourselves: 17 of 19 finished seasons were up in units, the lifetime football rate is 57.2% and the last five finished seasons are 58.3%, which match the three numbers on his sales page. The catch is that these are still his own season totals, with no individual picks, dates or odds anyone can check.
We found no independent buyer reviews at all, positive or negative, on CapperTek, TheRX, Reddit or Apple Podcasts. The only customer voices are testimonials the seller chose.
pricing_intro: We read the football picks page on 20 Nov 2026. It says "2026 Football Packages Available Now" but shows no package names or prices in its text. The page loads a PayPal hosted checkout button, and that checkout shows one fixed price item, listed below. The site's FAQ says members get "every premium selection we release" in football, basketball and baseball, but the only product on sale was football. We do not guess prices for anything else.
pricing: 30-Day NFL + College Football (PayPal checkout on the Football Picks page)
"Every premium football investment Payne's group makes during this 30-Day window is yours." All sales final, no refunds
Free picks and the Bet The Board newsletter
The podcast newsletter is free and promises "Additional Best Bets"; it is not the paid service
guarantee: There is no guarantee. The terms carry the heading "All Sales Are Final" with "No Refunds", and say the payment counts as "earned in full once you access the subscription-only area of this website." No refund is due "in the event your subscription/package is terminated, regardless of the reason for termination."

The terms also say the advice "is not guaranteed in terms of any type of performance" and that the site takes "a specific number of clients each season," so buying reserves a spot. Breaking the no resharing rule ends your account with no refund for unused time.

Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually much larger than the package price. At $579.99 for 30 days, a buyer staking $100 a DIME would need roughly six units of profit in the month just to cover the fee.

claims_note: How we checked: on 20 Nov 2026 we copied all 72 season lines from the records page and added them up. Before 2017 the page splits football into NFL and college football, so we combined the two for each season; from 2017 to 2018 on it shows one football combo line. We left out the separate win totals and futures lines. Each line's win rate matches its own wins and losses.

The three football headline numbers hold up on his own figures. In some seasons one half lost while the other carried it: college football was down 51.5 DIMES in 2011 to 2012 and 20.65 in 2014 to 2015, but the NFL side more than covered both.

Volume has fallen sharply. The football combo had 307 plays in 2018 to 2019 and 266 in 2022 to 2023, but only 98 in 2024 to 2025 and 89 in 2025 to 2026. Fewer plays means each season's percentage swings more.

Units are counted in "DIMES" on a 1 to 10 confidence scale, with an average released play of 2.2 DIMES since 2007, per the page. As a rough guide only: if every football play averaged 2.2 DIMES, the lifetime football profit of 963.78 DIMES over about 4,150 plays would be a return of roughly 10% of money risked, and the 2025 to 2026 season about 6.6%. Without the individual picks and their sizes we cannot compute it properly.

The other sports tell a mixed story: across every sport and season listed the page adds up to 5,162 wins and 3,981 losses, 56.5%, but baseball was 805 to 684 (54.1%) and stopped being reported after 2014, and college basketball was 1,060 to 874 (54.8%).
record: Watchdog search, 22 Nov 2026: we searched about 1.37 million captured public posts from X, Reddit, Covers, TheRX and other forums for Payne Insider plays that were posted or reposted before a game started. We found 78 posts naming Payne Insider, but none carried a play we could match to a game and grade.
What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. There is no pick by pick log with lines, odds and release times, and we found no third party tracker that has graded the paid plays.

What the seller publishes: season totals by sport from 2007 onward. Recent football combo seasons run from 50.8% (2019 to 2020, minus 34.44 DIMES) to 60.8% (2022 to 2023, plus 69.69 DIMES). The current 2026 to 2027 line read 38 wins, 31 losses and 1 push, plus 4.48 DIMES, on 20 Nov 2026, the same as four days earlier.

The early seasons carry the biggest numbers: 2008 to 2009 NFL shows 52 wins and 32 losses for plus 150.6 DIMES. Recent seasons are smaller and closer to break even, which a buyer judging the service today should weigh more than the lifetime figure.

TheRX forum keeps a list of services whose write ups members should not repost, and PayneInsider was on it in its February 2026 and 31 Oct 2026 service play threads. That tells us the paid plays circulate, but not how they perform.

The site's blog has not been updated since 2015, when it carried betting articles by guest writers. The Linktree page now points mainly to the podcast, a free newsletter, social accounts and the football picks page.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Payne Insider pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Payne Insider performs beyond our recount of the seller's own season totals.
our_data.context: For scale: the seller's football lines sit at 51% to 61% in recent seasons and 57.1% lifetime by our sum. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Payne Insider is almost nonexistent. The only buyer comments we found sit on the seller's own pages. Listener reviews of his free podcast are plentiful and warm, but they are about the show, not the paid picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Across CapperTek, TheRX, Sportsbook Review and Covers web searches, our saved copy of the main betting subreddits and Apple Podcasts, we found no independent post from anyone who says they bought Payne Insider picks, good or bad. The only customer voices are about 25 undated testimonials on his own site, all positive, praising steady profits, discipline and plays that move betting lines, two of them credited to Las Vegas oddsmakers including his podcast partner. On TheRX his write ups appear only on a do not repost list. On Apple Podcasts, listeners of the free Bet The Board show rate it 4.8 out of 5 from about 1,800 ratings and praise his candor, but none mention the paid service. There is no pattern of complaints, and also no independent praise of the paid picks, so a buyer has very little outside evidence either way.

The testimonials page shows about 25 notes signed with a first name and a place or job title, none dated. They describe winning months and seasons, renewals, a renewal discount and plays that move the betting line. One credits Payne as co founder of a Miami sports hedge fund group. Two are credited to Las Vegas oddsmakers, one of them his podcast co host. The seller picks what appears here, so it is not independent evidence.

The most recent listener reviews on Apple Podcasts, written when Bet The Board paused in 2025, thank both hosts, and one praises Payne's candor after more than a decade of listening. They are about the free podcast, not the paid picks.

CapperTek lists PayneInsider.com as an unverified, active service with "no reviews or complaints" on 20 Nov 2026. TheRX threads from February and October 2026 show the name only in the forum's do not repost list, with no comments on results.

A post search of r/sportsbook, r/sportsbetting and r/SportsBettingPicks in the Arctic Shift Reddit archive found no thread about the service, and our saved copy of the main betting subreddits has no buyer comment about it. Archive comment searches for the name timed out again on 20 Nov 2026, so Reddit comments were not fully checked.

conflicts: Payne co hosts Bet The Board, a free podcast whose new home on Sport & State has Hard Rock Bet as presenting sponsor, per Awful Announcing and Barrett Media. A sportsbook sponsor of the free show is a financial tie a buyer should know about, though it says nothing about the paid picks.
Todd Fuhrman, his podcast partner, is quoted as a testimonial on the paid site. That is not independent praise.
The site FAQ names offshore sportsbooks it prefers to use. We saw no sportsbook affiliate banners on the payneinsider.com pages we read.
strengths: A long running service that publishes season by season totals since 2007, and shows losing seasons as well as winning ones.
His three football headline numbers (17 of 19 winning seasons, 57.2% lifetime, 58.3% last five seasons) match his own season lines when we add them up.
The seller has a public face through a long running podcast with a known former oddsmaker, now on a new three year deal.
Terms are written out plainly, including the no refund rule.
Checkout runs through PayPal, which shows a clear fixed price before you pay.
concerns: No price appears in the page text; you only see $579.99 for 30 days inside the PayPal checkout.
All sales are final. No refund and no guarantee of any kind.
No pick by pick record, so the season totals and the closing line claim cannot be checked by anyone outside.
Play volume has dropped to under 100 football plays a season, and recent seasons are closer to break even than the lifetime numbers.
The operator gives no last name, company name, address or phone number, only an email address.
No independent buyer reviews exist that we could find; the only customer comments are seller chosen testimonials, one from his podcast partner.
Parts of the site are stale: the homepage still says 16 years, the blog stopped in 2015, and baseball and basketball records stop years ago.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds, the DIME size and the time it was sent. Season totals are not a record you can check.
Count units, not wins. Ask what one DIME means in dollars before you size bets off it, and work out how many units you need just to cover $579.99 a month.
Read the terms before you pay: all sales are final, and payment is earned the moment you log in.
Compare the current season line on the records page with what you actually receive, and keep the emails or texts with their time stamps.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. With under 100 plays a season, one season proves little.
faq: It is a real service that has sold football picks since at least 2007, run by the same Payne who co hosts the Bet The Board podcast. His published football season totals add up to the numbers he advertises, but they are his own totals with no pick by pick log, and we found no independent buyer reviews, complaints, or court or regulator action.

A professional bettor who uses the name Payne and keeps his last name private, per Awful Announcing. He co founded Bet The Board with former Caesars oddsmaker Todd Fuhrman; the show ran from 2014 to 2025 and returned on Clay Travis's Sport & State in August 2026. His site gives an email address only, with no company, address or phone.
How much does Payne Insider cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 the PayPal checkout behind the football picks page sold a 30 Day NFL + College Football package for $579.99. No other package or price was shown. The podcast and its newsletter are free.
No. The terms say all sales are final, payment is earned in full once you enter the members area, and no refund is due if a package ends early for any reason.
Does Payne Insider have a verified record?

No. The records page lists season totals by sport since 2007, including losing seasons, and our recount matches his football headline numbers. But there are no individual picks, dates or odds, and nobody independent has graded the paid plays that we could find.

You get a long running football service whose own numbers show more winning seasons than losing ones. What is unproven is whether a buyer betting at the lines they can actually get beats the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 by enough to cover $579.99 a month, and nothing refunds the package or your betting losses.
